messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 Incident detected: increased 429s from Hugging Face model-hosting during model pull phase. Affects model fetches for hosted + dedicated, cold starts failing. Severity: P1
maya: paging oncall — I'm on it. seeing a spike in cold-start failures in eu-west-1 and us-west-2.
sam: confirmed 429s from huggingface.co for multiple artifact downloads. retries are backing off. stack traces show HF 429 -> our fetcher gives up after 5 retries.
jin: observed cascading warmup failures: requests that normally trigger background prefetch are getting 429s and not cached. customer impact: slow responses and a subset of requests returning 503 when fallback isn't available.
pri: any known HF status page incident?
hf-status-bot: Hugging Face status: Degraded performance for model artifact downloads in multiple regions (https://status.huggingface.co/incident/abc123). Mitigation in progress.
leo: support queue: a handful of enterprise customers reporting higher error rates and increased latency. One customer (acme-corp) flagged real-time search indexer failures.
maya: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) expand fallback policy to compatible smaller checkpoint 2) enable local pre-warm using last-known-artifact cache 3) temporarily disable aggressive cold-start protection that denies low-replica spinups
sam: implementing (1) now — pushing config to route to quantized-ggml fallback for models with a compatible fingerprint. will post diff.
jin: I'll open a short-lived cache window: increase prefetch retries and jitter, but cap concurrency to avoid hitting HF harder. patch:
```json
{
  "prefetch": {"retries": 8, "retry_backoff_ms": [200,400,800,1600], "jitter": true, "max_concurrency": 6}
}
```
maya: let's also enable model-serving fallback: if primary artifact fails, switch to a smaller variant with a warning header to the app.
ashley: drafting customer comms template. we should quantify scope. Sam/Jin, can you estimate percent impacted and ETA for mitigation?
sam: current fetch success rate for artifact pulls dropped from 99.7% -> 86.4% over last 15m. Estimated impacted cold-start requests ~ 4.1% of total traffic (spikey).
jin: after increasing retries and lowering concurrency, fetch success rate improved to ~92% in last 5m. but still seeing intermittent 429 bursts.
maya: set incident channel to #oncall-handoff, escalate to eng-sre if repeated 10m bins of >5% cold-start errors.
pri: product impact note: streaming endpoints are mostly unaffected; batch/long-running jobs & new container startups hit this. Recommend pausing large prefetch sweeps for next 30m.
leo: support note added to customers: "We're experiencing degraded model artifact download performance from a third-party provider (Hugging Face). We're applying fallbacks and cache-warming; you may see transient errors while we mitigate. We'll update in 30 minutes."
hf-status-bot: Updated: Increased throttling observed. Estimated recovery unknown. Engineers are investigating.
sam: I filed an urgent ticket with HF support (ref HF-INC-8421) and requested rate-limit exceptions for us while they remediate. Sent logs and client fingerprints.
maya: rolling a temporary change: reduce background prefetch rate by 70% to remove flood traffic to HF. Jin, coordinate deploy?
jin: deploying canary change to prefetcher now. command: `kubectl apply -f prefetch-scaling-patch.yaml`
jin: canary looks good, prefetches down ~68% and cold-start error trend is flattening.
nashley: customer comms updated with a link to status page and support escalation contact.
pri: question: do we want to enable cached mirrors from our CDN for hot models as a longer-term mitigation? ops cost tradeoff but would reduce HF dependency.
sam: agree. created RFC ticket: INFRA-759 (mirror prefilling + signed artifact caching).
leo: support -> flagged top 10 customers to receive proactive notice and a mitigation checklist (fallback config + contact).
maya: oncall handoff in 45m to sam. leave a short runbook: 1) monitor hf-status, 2) if cold-start errors >5% for two consecutive 10m windows, escalate to eng-oncall and consider emergency full-pre-warm, 3) keep support messages updated.
sam: acknowledged, will take handoff.
hf-status-bot: Further update: rate limits being applied globally, mitigation underway.
maya: closing initial P1 -> moving to active mitigation state. will update post-handoff. :lock:
